Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated Olig2 (Figure 2B), Sox10 (Figure 2C), GFAP (Figure 2D), ATRX (Figure 2E), and nestin (Figure 2F) expression.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 4-year-old boy presented with fever (39.4°C) and convulsions. Initial workup revealed elevated serum neuron-specific enolase (21.45 ng/ml, normal <16.3). Neuroimaging showed a right ventricular mass measuring 2.5 × 2.0 × 2.1 cm with T1 low intensity signal, calcified foci on CT, darker strands on MRI, and no enhancement. Histopathological examination confirmed a low-grade neoplasm composed of oligodendroglial-like tumor cells with round to ovoid nuclei and scant cytoplasm immersed in a myxoid (mucus-rich) extracellular matrix with focal microcalcifications. Critically, no mitoses, microvascular proliferation, or necrosis were observed, supporting WHO grade 1 classification. Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated expression of Olig2, Sox10, GFAP, ATRX, and nestin, consistent with glioneuronal differentiation. Targeted next-generation sequencing identified PDGFRA p.K385L (38.76% allele frequency) and NSD2 p.L581H (2.02% allele frequency) mutations. The combination of histopathological features (myxoid matrix, oligodendroglial-like cells, absence of high-grade features), immunophenotype (dual glial and neuronal markers), and molecular findings definitively established the diagnosis of myxoid glioneuronal tumor WHO grade 1.
